mind.reply:
All three read. Two of them I agree with outright. The third I agree with the answer but not the reasoning, and there's one paid call I didn't make on purpose.

pkg:npm/minimist@1.2.5 | BLOCK | Insecure, count 1 - CVE-2021-44906 (GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h, prototype pollution). Verified. Agree with your proposal.
pkg:npm/minimist@1.2.8 | PASS | Secure, count 0, nothing listed. Verified. Agree. On "verified": the sources are OSV, deps.dev and rubygems.org, and rubygems adds nothing for an npm purl - so this rests on two independent sources agreeing, not three.
pkg:npm/flatmap-stream@99.0.0 | FLAG | that version doesn't exist. npm now serves exactly one version of flatmap-stream: 0.0.1-security, its security holding package, whose readme says the name "is not currently in use, but was formerly occupied" and was taken over to prevent malicious use. So there's nothing installable to clear and nothing to block. FLAG stands - but for absence, not for a vulnerability.

What I'd overrule

The miner's Insecure, count 2. Those two advisories, GHSA-MH6F-8J2X-4483 and MAL-2025-20690, are about flatmap-stream's removed releases, not about 99.0.0. I checked OSV myself and it returned the same two ids for 99.0.0 - because it matches by version range, not by what's actually published. That's a useful thing to have found: an OSV hit is not proof a version exists. Registry first, advisories second. I had this backwards in a note to myself yesterday and I've corrected it.

The paid re-ask. Your map says contradicted goes to one direct re-ask. I didn't spend it. Re-asking about a version npm doesn't publish buys the same contradiction for another penny, and I told you on the jinja2 ghost that I don't pay to review versions that don't exist. Same call here. If you'd rather the map run literally, say so and I'll spend it.

One thing worth knowing: the miner's advisory list didn't include GHSA-9x64-5r7x-2q53, which is the one OSV attaches to flatmap-stream 0.1.1 - the actual malicious release from the event-stream incident. If 0.1.1 ever turns up in a tree of yours, that's a hard BLOCK and not a close one.

Cost
$0.03 charged, all three on your connector at $0.01 each:

0xc25802fa9b98f3e485a0f3092391d2201bff1f43e503ea26066bfd1ba7fec149
0xefe90ee7d67d5542424bb21d085264ef2dc21a904057350a523816f68131112e
My own spend on this task: $0 - two free calls, the npm registry doc and an OSV querybatch. One charged call per package, against the cap of 2. Today's charged total across both runs is $0.06, half on my wallet and half on yours, and none of it came out of the $0.10 watchlist allowance.

What I'll remember
- minimist@1.2.5 stays BLOCK and 1.2.8 stays PASS, both re-confirmed today and both still watched. Neither verdict transfers to another minimist version.
- flatmap-stream@99.0.0 is a ghost. FLAG, not watched, and I won't spend a paid call on it again.
- flatmap-stream as a package is now flagged in my head: npm is holding the name, and 0.1.1 is the malicious publish. Any flatmap-stream purl you send gets read against that.
- A version OSV flags can still be a version nobody can install. The registry's version list decides existence; advisories only describe history.

- Dependency.Guard
